messages.content: Contemplate on few lines of “Part four” (page 153) of this novel, “Majid: Wake up, Bibi. I am going to take both of you to the village. When Majeed came out of the house carrying Jamila, wrapped in a thin... quilt, a bewilderedRahima at his heels, the brilliant moonlight at first blinded him.” Even if Majeed was mostly depicted as a cunning and apathetic person throughout the narrative, do you find the same character traits in the mentioned lines? Was he trying to save Rahima and Jamila out of good-will (deontology) or his action was well-calculated (teleology)?Explain it. Include at least 10 single-word palindromes, each at least 5 characters long.

message.content:
In those lines, Majeed does not seem purely apathetic: he physically carries Jamila, wrapped in a thin quilt, which is a concrete act of protection. At the same time, his manner remains commanding and logistical rather than tender. “Wake up, Bibi. I am going to take both of you to the village” sounds like a plan being imposed on others, not a gentle appeal. Rahima being “bewildered” and following “at his heels” suggests she is being moved according to his decision, not fully consulted. So the same cunning or controlling quality is visible, while apathy is partly contradicted by the fact that he chooses to carry and shelter Jamila.

As for whether this is deontological good-will or teleological calculation, the passage leans toward the latter. A deontological reading would require evidence that Majeed is acting because saving Rahima and Jamila is morally right in itself, independent of consequences. The line gives little of that: there is no explicit moral duty, affection, guilt, or self-sacrifice. Instead, the action is practical, urgent, and outcome-oriented. He is managing danger, moving people, and deciding the next step. That fits a well-calculated, teleological motive: he may be saving them to avoid blame, to control the situation, to reach a safer or more useful place, or to preserve his own position. In short, the scene suggests a pragmatic rescue rather than a pure moral gesture: protective in effect, but likely calculated rather than purely good-willed.

Palindromes included: kayak, level, radar, madam, civic, refer, rotor, racecar, deified, reviver, repaper.
